children: By Amanda Lee and P.R. Venkat
United Overseas Bank's net profit rose in the third quarter, as the lender set aside far less for potential bad loans than a year earlier.
Net profit for the three months ended September increased 182% from a year ago to 1.25 billion Singapore dollars, equivalent to US$975.55 million, the Singapore lender said Wednesday.

A year earlier, the bank's total allowances for credit and other losses were S$1.36 billion, including a pre-emptive provision of S$615 million in view of macroeconomic uncertainties and headwinds in U.S. and Greater China commercial real estate. This quarter, total allowances were only S$258 million.
Total income was S$3.38 billion, down 0.5% from a year earlier.

Net interest income--the difference between what banks earn on loans and pay on deposits--rose 1% to S$2.28 billion, despite net interest margin narrowing to 1.68% from 1.82% in a lower interest rate environment.
Net fee income rose 19% to S$733 million.
Other noninterest income fell 29% due to lower trading and investment income.
UOB is the first of Singapore's three major lenders to report earnings. DBS Group and Oversea-Chinese Banking Corp. are slated to report their results later this week.
